dehydrated_text:
Let me give you another example. I write books and have written three novels. You won't believe this, okay? But my wife knows how I work. You might think that when writing a book, one spends every day at the desk reading books, taking notes, and transforming them into a book, right? I don't do that. Instead, I lie in bed, play video games or read a book. Then, I walk to the park, come back with ideas, write them down for an hour or two on the computer. Exhausted from this, I run out of ideas and wonder, "Okay, tomorrow what am I going to do if I have no ideas? Can't write anymore." But the next day, I get up and have new ideas, writing them down again. So, it's not that I generate these ideas but receive them.

The way I teach now: when you see me teach, you might think I have a script or outline. I don't. I have a conception and framework in my head. I come to class and teach based on your observations, facial expressions, and responses. I access higher forces, receive information, and articulate it in class. Therefore, if you've been with me for 10 years, you'll notice I never teach the same class twice because each time, I channel a higher force.

Each experience is unique, like reading a book or seeing a great painting. You feel as though you are conversing with the universe when experiencing a good book. This book is a portal into the universe. If you want to be creative, trust the universe; if not, follow systems that destroy creativity because they teach an ineffective process. No scientist has ever come up with a great idea using the scientific method but through imagination and intuition.

I agree with your point about scientific methods being used to present ideas convincingly.
